Using functions to round to the nearest whole number (digits = 0 by default)
```{r}
round(3.14159)
```

Rounding to two decimal places (2 digits)
```{r}
round(3.14159, digits = 2)
```

Argument order
```{r}
print(rep(5, 7))

print(rep(x = 5, times = 7))
```

Character, numerical and logical variables
```{r}
x <- "this is a numerical variable"
print(x)
print(class(x))

y <- 6 * 10e-18
print(y)
print(class(y))

z <- TRUE
print(z)
print(class(z))
```

Using variables of different types
```{r}
cell_ID_1 <- "CX1"
cell_ID_2 <- "CX2"

treated_1 <- TRUE
treated_2 <- FALSE

num_cells_before_1 <- 5415
num_cells_before_2 <- 8123

num_cells_after_1 <- 1423
num_cells_after_2 <- 7543
```
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
```

Installing the tidyverse package collection for data science and from the gt package for visualising data frames.
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
```

Installing fortunes which gives a random number
```{r}
install.packages("fortunes")
```
```{r}
library(fortunes)
```

Exercise - Vectors
```{r}
cell_ids <- c(cell_ID_1, cell_ID_2)
treateds <- c(treated_1, treated_2)
n_before <- c(num_cells_before_1, num_cells_before_2)
n_after <- c(num_cells_after_1, num_cells_after_2)
```

Exercise - Indexing
```{r}
all_my_pets <- c("dog", "horse", "guinea pig", "chicken", "cat")
pet_4 <- all_my_pets[4]
print(pet_4)
```

Exercise - Creating a data frame
```{r}
radiation_experiment <- tibble(
  ID = cell_ids,
  treatment = treateds,
  cells_before = n_before,
  cells_after = n_after,
)

gt(radiation_experiment)

```
